Data Clean Rooms and Marketing Mix Modeling

Next-generation media marketing with Data Clean Rooms (DCR) and Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM)

Septeni Japan · Data Analyst · May 2025

Summary

This work combines a Data Clean Room (DCR) - a cloud environment provided by platforms in which data can be analysed together without exposing individual records - with Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) and causal inference, delivered through Septeni's XYhai solution. Hiroto Fukada designed and implemented the integrated architecture as a Data Analyst at Septeni Japan, and it was published as a solution article in May 2025.

The two halves answer different questions. MMM gives the strategic overview across online and offline media; the DCR supports detailed evaluation of individual tactics. Running them as one architecture means the same budget decision can be examined at both altitudes.

Why it matters

Third-party cookie restrictions have made user-level tracking progressively less reliable, while advertisers still need to know which media actually moved the outcome. The requirement is usually stated as a trade-off: effective marketing measurement on one side, privacy protection on the other.

Treating it as a trade-off is the mistake. Measurement that depends on identifying individuals is not only a privacy liability, it is also fragile - it degrades with every platform policy change. Aggregate, model-based measurement that never needs the individual record is the more durable answer, and it is the one that survives the next restriction.

Results

The integrated DCR + MMM architecture analyses initiatives across online and offline channels inside a privacy-protected environment, and supports data-driven budget allocation from those results. Cross-media ROI can be evaluated without identifying individual users, and budget optimisation is unified across online and offline media.

The approach was published as a solution article in May 2025, which describes how clarifying the causal relationships between marketing initiatives is what makes integrated optimisation possible.
